links.comparator_used: Pre-implementation period (2006-2014) without the potassium CDSS, compared with the post-implementation period (2014-2023)
links.outcome: Proportion of drug-related adverse events involving potassium salts
links.effect: Proportion involving potassium fell from 2.8% in 2013 to 0.2% in 2023 (p = 0.008); 64 of 9,308 drug-related adverse events (0.7%) involved potassium salts, while overall drug-related events increased (p < 0.001).
links.tradeoff: 42.9% of 90,741 potassium prescriptions (38,961) triggered blocked attempts, with an upward trend (β = 20.4, p < 0.001). Near-miss prescriptions stayed high (median 27.4%, IQR 17.5-32.2). The authors suggest possible alert fatigue, overreliance on the CDSS and override practices.
links.quote: Despite an increase in overall drug-related events (p < 0.001), the proportion involving potassium decreased from 2.8% in 2013% to 0.2% in 2023 (p = 0.008).

design_hint: hard-stop CDSS blocking prescriptions exceeding potassium safety limits
